text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Darkfield_microscopy_of_lesion_exudate
Given the mother's lack of prenatal care and history of STIs, I need to rule out congenital syphilis despite the negative RPR, so please test the lesion fluid directly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative infectious workup, I suspect an autoimmune etiology. Does the rash have a "collar of scale" appearance, and did the mother have any autoimmune conditions like lupus or Sjogren's syndrome?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The sparing of the palms and soles and the presence of pustules on an erythematous base in a 4-day-old strongly suggest Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum. I will request clinical images to confirm the characteristic appearance of the rash.
